components.why: Pipfile at repository root declares [packages] and [requires] python_version='3.7', establishing a Python project boundary. No setup.py or pyproject.toml is present, so no formal package name is declared; the root component is named (root) per the labeling convention.

deployables.name: web
deployables.why: Procfile line 1: 'web: gunicorn autoapp:app -b 0.0.0.0:$PORT -w 3' declares a web process type binding the application via gunicorn. This is the Heroku-style process declaration analogous to a Compose service; labeled as kind=service per the closest MAP.md vocabulary match.

capabilities.why: requirements/prod.txt declares psycopg2, the PostgreSQL adapter for Python; conduit/settings.py ProdConfig (line ~36) uses SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI defaulting to 'postgresql://localhost/example', confirming PostgreSQL as the production datastore.
requirements/prod.txt declares Flask-JWT-Extended and PyJWT; conduit/app.py line ~10 imports JWTManager from flask_jwt_extended and registers it as a Flask extension.
requirements/prod.txt:4 SQLAlchemy==1.1.9 and Pipfile:8 sqlalchemy; a relational ORM, labeled the same way as SQLAlchemy in the golden superset labels

requirements/prod.txt Flask-JWT-Extended and PyJWT dependencies; JWT auth is registered in conduit/app.py.

components.why: Pipfile and requirements files establish a Python project boundary but no formal package name is declared (no setup.py or pyproject.toml). The conduit/ sub-directory contains the application package but there is no separate component manifest for it.

deployables.why: The Procfile web process is labeled. The map vocabulary does not have an explicit Procfile kind; 'service' is the closest available kind. There is no Dockerfile in this repository.

interfaces.why: The Procfile binds to $PORT (a dynamic environment variable), not a static port number. No Dockerfile EXPOSE or compose ports declaration is present in oracle files, so no declared_port interface can be labeled.

capabilities.why: psycopg2 (PostgreSQL) and Flask-JWT-Extended/PyJWT (JWT auth) are labeled. Flask-SQLAlchemy (ORM) and Flask-Bcrypt (password hashing) are declared in requirements but lack clear single-capability catalog mappings and are noted below. The full dependency list was not exhaustively mapped.

edges.why: uses_capability edges for labeled capabilities are included. No local component dependencies or build/run relationships exist in this single-component project.

notes: This repository has no setup.py or pyproject.toml; the Pipfile and requirements/prod.txt establish the Python dependency context but do not assign a project name. The component is labeled (root).

Flask-SQLAlchemy and SQLAlchemy are declared in requirements/prod.txt; they are an ORM layer over the PostgreSQL database declared by psycopg2. A separate datastore:relational label is not added because the specific driver (psycopg2) already establishes datastore:postgresql unambiguously.
Flask-Bcrypt (password hashing) and Flask-Caching (in-memory cache, CACHE_TYPE='simple') are declared but do not match any catalog capability name; they are noted here.
The Pipfile [requires] python_version='3.7' is a runtime requirement; it would appear in the component's runtime_requirements property per MAP.md if the map supports Pipfile.
conduit/settings.py DevConfig uses SQLite (sqlite:///dev.db); this is a development-only configuration and is not labeled as a separate capability per the oracle scope.
The Procfile 'web' process entry is the primary deployment declaration; its gunicorn binding uses $PORT so no static port can be labeled.
